Q: How to calculate sum of subsequent rows in a dataframe changing the reference row under condition A:

In base R we could do

fx_base <- function(dfi) {
  n <- nrow(dfi)
  out <- dfi
  # out$ID_n <- ave(out$ID, out$ID, FUN=seq_along)  ## optional
  d <- unclass(as.Date(out$date_ric))
  keep <- integer(n)
  diff_dd <- integer(n)
  a <- d[1L]
  id <- out$ID[1L]
  keep[1L] <- 1L
  if (n > 1L) {
    for (i in 2L:n) {
      if (out$ID[i] != id) {
        id <- out$ID[i]
        a <- d[i]
        keep[i] <- 1L
        next
      }
      di <- d[i] - a
      diff_dd[i] <- di
      if (di >= 28L) { keep[i] <- 1L; a <- d[i] }
    }
  }
  out$keep <- keep
  out$diff.dd <- diff_dd
  out
}

Q: How to recursively get SAS dataset creation dates on Linux with NOXCMD (Pipe disabled)? A:

When NOXCMD disables pipes, you cannot recursively retrieve SAS dataset creation dates on Linux. You can instead query metadata using PROC CONTENTS or DICTIONARY tables to retrieve creation datetimes programmatically.

Q: Old GoogleMaps CocoaPod (2.7.0) keeps getting re-added despite upgrading to 8.4.0 A:

This is coming from your cn1lib which is out of date. It pushes the update. It seems from your question here that you're using an old project and probably an old cn1lib.

Migrating to maven and a maven dependency would solve the issue and remove the need to set these explicitly.

Q: Canonical version of Noreturn macro for pre-C11 A:

As of 2026, portable code requires something like:

#if defined(__has_c_attribute)
#  if __has_c_attribute(noreturn)
#    define NORETURN [[noreturn]]
#  endif
#endif

#if !defined(NORETURN) && defined(__has_cpp_attribute)
#  if __has_cpp_attribute(noreturn)
#    define NORETURN [[noreturn]]
#  endif
#endif

#if !defined(NORETURN) && defined(__has_attribute)
#  if __has_attribute(noreturn)
#    define NORETURN __attribute__((noreturn))
#  endif
#endif

#if !defined(NORETURN)
#  if defined(__STDC_VERSION__) && (__STDC_VERSION__ >= 201112L)
#    define NORETURN _Noreturn
#  elif defined(_MSC_VER)
#    define NORETURN __declspec(noreturn)
// I am taking user 0___________’s word for this one:
#  elif defined(__IAR_SYSTEMS_ICC__) || defined(__ICCARM__)
#    define NORETURN __noreturn
#  else
#    define NORETURN /**/
#endif

The /**/ expands to a whitespace token, which is safer than #define noreturn.

Unfortunately, right now GCC is the only major compiler that supports #if defined(__has_c_attribute) && __has_c_attribute(noreturn). All compilers do support short-circuiting for non-function-like macros, such as #if defined(__STDC_VERSION__) && (__STDC_VERSION__ >= 201112L). Therefore, you cannot yet portably write:

#if defined(__has_c_attribute) && __has_c_attribute(noreturn)
#  define NORETURN [[noreturn]]
#elif defined(__has_cpp_attribute) && __has_cpp_attribute(noreturn)
#  define NORETURN [[noreturn]]
#elif defined(__has_attribute) && __has_attribute(noreturn)
#  define NORETURN __attribute__((noreturn))
#elif defined(__STDC_VERSION__) && (__STDC_VERSION__ >= 201112L)
#  define NORETURN _Noreturn
#elif defined(_MSC_VER)
#  define NORETURN __declspec(noreturn)
/* ... */
#else
#  define NORETURN /**/
#endif

The Standard really ought to make this extension official.
